newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court annuls Council rules on visas.
newsitem.headline: Court annuls Council rules on visas.

text.p: The European Court of Justice annulled on Tuesday the Council of the European Union's regulation governing visa requirements for third party nationals entering the European Union.

Recognizing the necessity to maintain legal certainty, the court told states to keep the regulation in effect until the Council takes the necessary steps to clear the legislation with the European Parliament.

The court agreed the Council failed to consult Parliament a second time after making substantive amendments to the European Commission's proposal, as required under the Communitiy legislative process, before adopting the regulation.

The substantive differences between the Commission proposal and the regulation adopted by the Council include: the proposal suggested a defined list of third countries needing visas but the regulation lets states expand the list; the number of non-member countries on the list was reduced from 126 to 98; and mutual recognition of visas by member states was abandoned.

application for annulment of Council regulation (EEC) No 2317/95 determining the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external frontiers of the member states
1. Annuls Council regulation (EEC) No 2317/95 determining the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external frontiers of the member states;
2. Declares that the effects of the annulled regulation are to be maintained until the Council of the European Union has adopted new legislation in the matter;
3. Orders the Council to pay the costs;
4. Orders the French Republic to bear its own costs.
